text:
crowfoot — a demo

This is the database behind nivoca, a Japanese vocabulary app.
The version drawn here is its legacy build: Next.js + Supabase, shipped as a PWA.
The app has since been rebuilt on Flutter with a Kotlin/Spring backend, and this
earlier codebase was opened as github.com/Junjak-Personal/nivoca-legacy.

23 tables · 27 foreign keys, parsed straight from 37 Supabase migration files:
    npx crowfoot erd build --input 'migrations/*.sql' --format postgres

Everything you see is editable

Add ?edit=1 to the URL. Without it the diagram is read-only on purpose, so a
link you share cannot be rearranged by whoever opens it.

Drag tables to move them. Drag across empty canvas — or Ctrl/Cmd-click — to
select several at once, then move, tint or delete them together.

Grouping

Select the tables you want, right-click one of them, and choose to group them.
A named, tinted box is drawn behind the members — the box is derived from where
they sit, so it follows them. Drag the group label to move the whole set.

A table may belong to more than one group. The toolbar switches between group
view and a plain alphabetical list without touching the data.

Memos and colour

Ctrl/Cmd + right-click empty canvas to drop a memo like this one. Memos resize,
recolour, change font size, and copy-paste — including into another browser tab.

Tables, memos and groups all take a tint from the same 12-colour palette, so the
diagram stays consistent with the app it documents.

Making an arrangement permanent

Your layout lives in the URL, which makes it shareable but not durable. Copy the
?edit=1 URL and turn it into files the viewer loads on every visit:

    npx crowfoot erd from-link --input '<the URL>' --output-dir dist

That writes layout.json, memos.json and groups.json next to schema.json. Commit
them, and this arrangement is what everyone sees — this demo included.

Where this runs

A static site: no server, no database connection. crowfoot parses the schema once
and emits HTML, CSS and JSON you can host anywhere — S3, nginx, GitHub Pages.
This page is nginx on a mini PC behind a Cloudflare tunnel.

github.com/Junjak-Personal/crowfoot   ·   npm i -g crowfoot
